messages:
alex: quick heads-up — I want to run a tiling bench on staging to validate tiny-window continuous-batching behavior. planning a 4h sweep across max_tokens {64,128,256}, batch_cap {8,16,32}, and window_ms {8,12,20}. can ppl answer a couple quick Qs before I schedule?

maria: go ahead with the plan, but we should lock preemptive-eviction to 'on' for the 256 runs to avoid KV growth. otherwise the tail latencies will contaminate results.

chris: +1 for the sweep. curious if you want to include a run with kv-cache disabled as a control? last time tiling + small windows showed weird 99p spikes when cache warmed slowly.

alex: good call. include one control per max_tokens with kv-cache disabled (so 3 extra runs). thanks.

jon: FYI CI load generator has a new patch that better simulates short bursts. use the flag `--burst-profile short-bursty` if you want more realistic frontend traffic.

alex: ideal — will use it. quick question on instrumentation: which histograms should I push to bench results bucket? want to make sure perf dashboards pick up the right traces.

maria: send 50p/90p/99p/99.9p for token latency, and per-request total latency. also push batch-size distribution and active-queue-length. tag runs with `tiling:yes` and `window_ms:<value>`.

alex: copy. loadgen cmd I'll run (example):
```
./loadgen \
  --model rdx-13b-q4\
  --concurrency 8 \
  --prompt-file samples/tiling_small_prompts.json \
  --max_tokens 128 \
  --window_ms 12 \
  --batch_cap 16 \
  --kv_cache on \
  --burst-profile short-bursty \
  --push-metrics bench.bucket/tiling_runs
```

chris: small nit — add `--warmup-requests 500` to reduce warm-start noise. and set `--seed 42` so runs are comparable.

alex: will do. also want to experiment with a "preemptive max_tokens" knob where we cap the request tokens allowed in the queue to avoid very long requests blocking small ones. any objections if I set that to 192 for the 256 runs?

maria: that's the plan we discussed. set preemptive_max_tokens=192 for the 256 runs. annotate in metadata so we can see difference.

jon: one more — can we run a tiny 30m sanity on canary first (single GPU) to make sure we don't thrash infra? after that, escalate to 4h multi-GPU.

alex: will run 30m canary at 02:00 PT, then schedule 4h sweep at 03:00 PT if no issues. tagging @eng-oncall in case it trips alerts.

ci-bot: deploy job queued: `bench-tiling-canary-2723456789` -> started on staging/gpu-a10x1 (logs: https://ci.internal/redwood/bench-tiling-canary-2723456789).

chris: looking at the quick log tail — small increase in mem during canary but within safety. good to proceed.

maria: I'll start the multi-GPU run at 03:00 PT and pin config in bench/tiling/2026-03-17 with a short readme describing knobs. alex — please add the expected result matrix in the PR so we know pass/fail criteria.

alex: will open PR now with matrix and expected thresholds (90p < 120ms, 99p < 300ms for window <=12ms, tolerance flags for 256 run with preemptive cap).

jon: ping me if you want me to own alert silences for the 4h window. happy to mute noisy SLOs.

alex: thanks — if anyone sees anything odd during the sweep drop a note here. i'll post the raw artifacts and a short summary after the run. :thumbsup:
